description.narrative: Domestic revenue mobilization (DRM) is a key part of Oxfam Denmark’s strategy and programming and there is a strong alignment between the priorities of the call and Oxfam Denmark’s ambitions. In the organisational strategy 2023-2027 Economic Justice is one of four intervention areas with ambitions on promotion of tax justice and advocacy for pro-poor and gender-transformative public investments. This project would contribute to realizing outcome 1.2 of the Danida Strategic Partnership global results framework “Local and national governments, private sector and other key decision makers increase pro-poor, gender transformative and social spending and quality public services based on resource mobilization and fiscal justice in response to advocacy by civilsociety.” Under the Danida SP, activities relating to outcome 1.2 and DRM are taking place in nine countries as well as at regional (Africa and Latin America) and global levels. The budget for DRM activities from Danida SP in 2024 and 2025 amounts to 21million DKK. Oxfam Denmark receives funding in 2023-2025 from Norad for a project which aims to strengthen the capacity of civil society and investigative journalists to push for fiscal justice in Ghana, Uganda and Kenya and regionally in Africa, therebyaligning closely with this top-up project. The grant is co-financed with Danida SP funding and reported on in the annual Results Report 2023. The top-up project will complement theongoing and planned activities by expanding the reach and deepening the engagement with civil society actors and policy makers at national, regional and global levels. In particular, this project will strengthen the preparations and engagement of African civil society in relevant regional and global processes (outcome 3), thereby building on ongoing activities in the three focus countries. Inthe ToC for Ghana, activities under outcome 1.1 include support to citizen groups and CSOs to call for and influence fair tax reforms as well as extractive sector fiscal policy reforms.In the ToC for Uganda, activities under outcome 1.2 support citizen demand forfiscal justice including progressive and gender sensitive DRM at local and national level. In the ToC for Kenya, activities under outcome 1.1 seek to increase DRM and pro-poorspending through support to actions of citizens, CSOs, media and oversight independent bodies.

participating-org.narrative: Center for Budget and Tax Policy

HISTORY:
Founded in 2015 as a company limited by guarantee, the Centre for Budget and Tax Policy (CBTP) is an independent, not-for-profit think tank and centre of excellence in Africa on budget and tax policy. CBTP is headquartered in Kampala, Uganda and seeks to provide a platform for advocacy and capacity building for CSO/ PSO, government agencies and development partner organisations in governance and accountability. The centre focuses on enhancing prudent and all-inclusive public finance management prac¬tices in public institutions to promote equitable development nationally, on the continent and beyond.
ACHIEVEMENTS;
1. Improved management of public resources during emergencies and fragile situations. We specifically influenced public policy decisions on Uganda’s COVID-19 responses by advocating for provision of support of vulnerable persons in Uganda and supporting of businesses. 2. Successfully convened citizens and stakeholders on tax policy and social protection at both national and international level. For-example, CBTP hosteda session during the World Bank-IMF Annual Meeting 2020. 3. Contributed to provision of alternative proposals to government on efficient and effective budget allocations particularly for financing social services frontline sectors; Education, Health, Agriculture and Social Development. CBTP regularly engage the relevant committees of Parliament especially during budget processing. 4. Improving access to social protection interventions for vulnerable groups in Uganda.
INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE;
Mission: To be a global think-tank that advances society through rigorous research, analysis of budget, tax policy for the promotion of equity, justice, accountability, and democracy.
Institutional objectives:
•To provide well researched, rigorous, and conceptualised bud¬get and tax policy analysis in Africa • To inform and shape debate on budget and tax policy to influ¬ence outcomes. • To provide a robust, reliable, effective and interactive platform for multi-stakeholder engagement on budget and tax policy issues • To advocate for equity budgetingand tax justice in Africa and beyond • To advocate for efficient allocation and proper utilization of public resources to enhance economic development • Advocate for the formulation of public finance manage¬ment policies and tax policy laws that are responsive tothe needs of the society • To advocate for inclusion of gender, climate change, human rights issues in the budget and tax policy discourse • To provide analysis on all forms of public policy issues that have a nexus with social justice, accountability, democracy and sustainable development.
Field(s) of activity: What are the principal thematic and geographic areas in which the organization works?
1. Governance and Accountability 2. Health 3. Education 4. Agriculture 5. Energy and Environment 6. Physical Infrastructure 7. Inclusive Social and Economic Development 8. Social Protection policy and financing
